title: Netanyahu Said Israel 'Still Has Something to Do' in Lebanon at Muni Expo on 24 June. Hours Earlier, Katz Said There Is 'No American Demand to Withdraw.' Leiter Then Told the Fifth Round of Washington Talks It Was a 'Train Wreck.' Bennett Said Soldiers in Lebanon Are 'Handcuffed.' All on the Same Day, All on Record
narrative:
On 24 June 2026, at the Muni Expo conference in Tel Aviv, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared that Israel still had 'something to do' in Lebanon and defended plans for a security belt along the border. Hours later, the IDF carried out a fresh strike inside southern Lebanon targeting a vehicle near the Ali al-Taher Ridge that the IDF said 'was deemed a threat to IDF soldiers.' The Air Force struck the vehicle 'in order to remove the threat.' This was the second IDF strike reported within hours.

Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz claimed in a separate interview at a convention of local leaders in Tel Aviv that 'there is no American demand for Israel to withdraw from Lebanon.' Katz described the absence of a US withdrawal demand as 'a diplomatic achievement.' The comments came as Israeli and Lebanese representatives resumed US-mediated talks in Washington — the fifth round — scheduled to continue for three days at both political and military levels.

Israeli Ambassador to the United States Yechiel Leiter told the Washington meeting that the process was at risk of derailment: 'This is the fifth round of talks, and I have to say, we are in a train wreck.' Leiter's full quote: 'Four rounds ago, we all boarded the same train. We sat in the same car and traveled toward the same destination, with the U.S. serving as the locomotive. The train was heading in a very clear direction: full peace between the countries, Iran out and its malign influence out of Lebanon; the dismantling of Hezbollah; peace and security for Lebanon and Israel. Today, that train is at risk of coming off the rails. I hope we can put it back on track.'

Israeli opposition leader Naftali Bennett publicly accused Israeli soldiers stationed in Lebanon of being 'handcuffed.' Netanyahu sent a direct message to US President Donald Trump, stating that he would be unable to implement any instructions regarding troop withdrawal from Lebanon and advising the White House against issuing such directives to avoid political clashes.

analysis:
Three findings structure the 24 June Israel-Lebanon diplomatic layer, and each one names a specific evidentiary layer that the prior Lebanon articles did not contain.

First, the both-sides-on-record contradiction on US withdrawal pressure. Katz publicly states there is 'no American demand for Israel to withdraw from Lebanon' and frames this as 'a diplomatic achievement.' The fifth round of US-mediated talks is currently underway in Washington. The Lebanese delegation's stated goal is securing 'a clear timetable for the Israeli withdrawal' and full deployment of the Lebanese army south of the Litani River. The US as mediator is between Israel's 'no withdrawal' position and Lebanon's 'immediate withdrawal timetable' position. Katz's 'no American demand' framing implies the US has privately aligned with Israel against Lebanon's demand, but no public US statement corroborates this. The structural contradiction: the US as mediator is publicly pushing a process whose Israeli participant claims is being conducted on US-aligned terms, while the Lebanese participant (and the US-brokered Article 1 of the MoU) frames the same process as conditional on Israeli withdrawal.

Second, Leiter's 'train wreck' admission is the most explicit on-record acknowledgement from a senior Israeli negotiator that the talks are derailing. The Israeli ambassador to the United States — the senior Israeli negotiator at the table — publicly described the talks as 'a train wreck' on day one of the fifth round. Leiter's full metaphor — 'Four rounds ago, we all boarded the same train. We sat in the same car and traveled toward the same destination, with the U.S. serving as the locomotive. The train was heading in a very clear direction: full peace between the countries, Iran out and its malign influence out of Lebanon; the dismantling of Hezbollah; peace and security for Lebanon and Israel. Today, that train is at risk of coming off the rails' — concedes that the previously shared destination ('Iran out and its malign influence out of Lebanon; the dismantling of Hezbollah') is no longer reachable on the current trajectory. This is structurally incompatible with Katz's 'diplomatic achievement' framing of the same day.

Third, Netanyahu's 'something to do' plus the Trump letter is the most explicit on-record framing of the Israeli intent to continue operations while refusing any withdrawal framework. Netanyahu publicly declares more Lebanon operations at Muni Expo on 24 June while simultaneously sending Trump a private message that he 'would be unable to implement any instructions regarding troop withdrawal from Lebanon' and advising the White House against issuing such directives to avoid political clashes. The Israeli public posture: more strikes + no withdrawal + ambassador warns talks are in a train wreck + Bennett says soldiers are handcuffed. The Israeli private posture to Trump: cannot implement withdrawal even if asked. The convergence of all four — Netanyahu, Katz, Leiter, Bennett — on the same calendar day is the load-bearing fact.

Fourth, Bennett's 'handcuffed' framing is the rare instance of an Israeli opposition leader publicly contradicting the sitting government on operational conduct in an active war zone. Bennett's accusation that soldiers are 'handcuffed' is contradicted by Netanyahu's and Katz's repeated public responses, and by a new written directive stating that the Israeli army will respond to any threat that emerges on the ground. Bennett's framing aligns with the prior 'Katz-free-to-act-vs-IDF-spokesperson' contradiction (21 June Burgenstock opening day article): the operational rules of engagement are not aligned between ministers, spokespersons, opposition leaders, or the written directive.

Fifth, the pilot framework and the phased mechanism. Israeli officials told Ynet that they are discussing a US-backed pilot framework under which Israeli forces would gradually transfer control of parts of southern Lebanon to the Lebanese Armed Forces, but only after the Lebanese army undergoes US-supervised training and vetting to ensure they are not linked to Hezbollah. Al-Akhbar reported Israeli proposals envision a phased, step-by-step mechanism: local clearing of Hezbollah infrastructure, followed by limited Israeli withdrawals, then expansion to larger areas over time. Israel is demanding that the Lebanese army prove it can dismantle Hezbollah infrastructure before any Israeli withdrawal from border areas, including by inspecting tunnels in the Ali al-Taher area. An American source told Al Arabiya Israel and Lebanon do not maintain diplomatic relations and remain formally in a state of conflict.

Sixth, Hezbollah's 'blatant violation' framing and Iran's warning. Hezbollah condemned the 24 June bulldozer shooting as a 'blatant violation of the ceasefire' and emphasized that it had adhered to the agreement since implementation. Ali Bahreini, Iran's envoy, had warned on Tuesday that violations of the ceasefire framework risked derailing broader diplomatic progress. The 24 June strike is the third Day-N incident in the post-ceasefire sequence (after Day 2's 16-fatality incident on 20 June and the bulldozer shooting on 24 June). The UNIFIL observation on 23 June — 'no launches, strikes or interceptions since Sunday, marking more than two days without such activity' — was overtaken by the 24 June bulldozer shooting.

The load-bearing contradiction: Israel simultaneously demands that Lebanon prove it can dismantle Hezbollah before any withdrawal AND insists there is 'no American demand for Israel to withdraw' AND publicly declares more strikes are coming AND the senior Israeli negotiator admits the talks are 'a train wreck.' The fifth round of talks was launched on the explicit US premise that ending the Lebanon war is integral to the broader ceasefire, per Article 1 of the MoU signed between the US and Iran.

Beat-distinct from prior Israel-Lebanon articles (Day-2 16-killed, Nabatieh bulldozer shooting, Katz free-to-act IDF spokesperson contradiction). Those articles covered specific kinetic incidents. This article covers the diplomatic-credibility layer at the parallel Washington talks, the Leiter 'train wreck' admission, and the Bennett-vs-Netanyahu internal political pressure — all 24 June specific.
verdict: On 24 June 2026, four senior Israeli figures — Netanyahu, Katz, Leiter, and Bennett — publicly contradicted each other on the same day on the core question of whether Israel should or will withdraw from Lebanon. Netanyahu at Muni Expo said Israel still has 'something to do'; Katz at a separate Tel Aviv event said there is 'no American demand for Israel to withdraw' and called the absence 'a diplomatic achievement'; Leiter at the fifth-round Washington talks called the process 'a train wreck' and said 'Today, that train is at risk of coming off the rails'; Bennett publicly accused Israeli soldiers in Lebanon of being 'handcuffed'; and Netanyahu sent Trump a private message saying he would be 'unable to implement any instructions regarding troop withdrawal' and advised the White House against issuing such directives. The convergence on a single calendar day is the load-bearing finding. Israel is simultaneously demanding that Lebanon prove it can dismantle Hezbollah before any withdrawal AND publicly declaring more strikes are coming AND publicly warning the US-mediated talks are derailing. The fifth round of talks was launched on the explicit US premise that ending the Lebanon war is integral to the broader ceasefire, per Article 1 of the US-Iran MoU. Beat-distinct from the Nabatieh bulldozer-shooting Day-3 incident (kinetic, specific shooting), the Katz-free-to-act-vs-IDF-spokesperson contradiction (21 June), and the 84-violations + Trump public rebuke of Netanyahu (17 June). This is the 24 June diplomatic-credibility layer covering the Leiter 'train wreck' admission and the Netanyahu-Trump private-message refusal to implement any withdrawal directive.
